paragraphs: Shimon ha-Pakuli. Rashi explains: a seller of cotton wool. The Arukh explains pakuli as clean flax. In the Zohar, he was called Pakuli from פקו פליליה [paku pelilah, “they stumble in judgment,” read in the Zohar as a play on release from judgment], for he brought his father out of the judgment of Gehinnom. He arranged the eighteen blessings before Rabban Gamliel the Elder at Yavneh: Berakhot 28, end of side b. In Megillah 17b: before Rabban Gamliel at Yavneh, without mentioning “the Elder.” It appears that Yuhasin is right: he arranged them before Rabban Gamliel the Elder. Although Tosafot, Niddah, first chapter, 6b, write that ordinarily Rabban Gamliel the Elder is not mentioned simply as Rabban Gamliel, but as Rabban Gamliel the Elder, here it must mean Rabban Gamliel the Elder. For the wording of the foregoing Gemara, Berakhot, is: the rabbis taught, Shimon ha-Pakuli arranged the eighteen blessings in order before Rabban Gamliel at Yavneh. Rabban Gamliel asked the sages, “Is there anyone who knows how to institute the blessing concerning the Sadducees?” Shmuel the Small stood and instituted it. The next year he forgot it, and considered it for two or three hours, but they did not remove him. Thus it implies that at the very time Shimon ha-Pakuli arranged the eighteen blessings, Rabban Gamliel asked whether anyone knew how to institute the blessing concerning the Sadducees. It is known that Rabban Gamliel the Elder eulogized Shmuel the Small; see his entry. Therefore Shimon ha-Pakuli arranged the eighteen blessings before Rabban Gamliel the Elder, even though it says simply Rabban Gamliel. Moreover, before his death Shmuel the Small prophesied the killing of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel and R' Yishmael the high priest, who were killed at the destruction, whereas Rabban Gamliel of Yavneh lived after the destruction.
